subject: Checkpoint AI: Request to validate fallback window and partial SLA credit
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan@checkpoint.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2029-06-12T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden latency spike during checkpoint fallback - request to validate window and credit

Hi David / Laura,

We observed a material latency increase and a handful of failed requests in our Checkout flow between 2029-06-11T23:42:00Z and 2029-06-12T00:10:00Z (UTC). Our SLOs are being impacted and finance is asking whether this qualifies for a partial SLA credit under our contract.

Symptoms we saw:
- 95th percentile latency rose from ~180ms to ~1.2s for token-generation endpoints (short burst).
- ~0.9% 5xx error rate for the same window.
- Our tracing shows a server-side model cold-start path where a checkpointing fallback triggered extra KV-load on the instance.

What we need from Redwood:
1) Confirmation of the exact availability/latency window you see on your side (start/end) and whether this falls under an SLA-eligible incident.
2) Raw trace bundle and a short postmortem or planned timeline for an RCA.
3) A rough estimate of credit or a proposed compensatory approach so we can brief procurement (we can share usage numbers if needed).

I've attached a telemetry snapshot from our side (telemetry_snapshot_20290612.json) and a short trace snippet in the zip. Happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Thanks,
Jordan Lee
Head of Platform, Checkpoint AI
jordan@checkpoint.ai

Attachment: telemetry_snapshot_20290612.json (sample), checkpoint_fallback_traces.zip (trace snippets)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan@checkpoint.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-06-12T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike during checkpoint fallback - request to validate window and credit

Jordan —

Thanks for the detailed notes and the artifacts. We’re looking into this now. Initial notes from our telemetry team: there was a short sequence where autoscaler rebalanced a small fraction of your routed instances while a background checkpoint write coincided with an unexpected eviction on a single host. That combination can trigger longer tail latencies and sporadic 5xx responses.

Next steps from Redwood:
- I’ve asked infra to export the server-side traces for 2029-06-11T23:30:00Z through 2029-06-12T00:30:00Z and we’ll share the bundle.
- Laura (CC’d) will lead the eligibility assessment vs. the SLA and pull the policy exceptions if any.
- Marissa (CC’d, billing) — please advise on the shape of a provisional credit calculation so Jordan’s procurement can plan.

Can you confirm whether the user-impacting transactions were all routed to the token-generation endpoint or if embeddings endpoints were affected too? That helps us scope the impact.

I’ll follow up within 24 hours with the exported traces and an eligibility intent.

— David
David Kim
Senior Account Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan@checkpoint.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-06-13T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike during checkpoint fallback - request to validate window and credit

Hi Jordan, David —

We’ve completed a preliminary eligibility sweep based on the contract (section 4.2: Availability & Remedies). Summary:
- Confirmed incident window from server logs: 2029-06-11T23:41:50Z to 2029-06-12T00:12:05Z (UTC).
- Impact: elevated 95p latency and 5xx spike consistent with transient host eviction and concurrent checkpointing write (matches your traces).
- Root cause hypothesis (prelim): concurrent checkpoint write + eviction led to temporary KV cache misses and one instance routing retries.

Based on the computed availability delta (we use token-weighted averaging across affected endpoints), the provisional credit estimate is 3.6% of June monthly consumption. That’s preliminary pending a full RCA and exact token tallies (we’ll include the request-level weighting).

Attachments: I uploaded the server trace bundle and a working spreadsheet with the calculation (proposed_credit_calc.xlsx) to the linked Drive folder.

Proposed timeline:
- Friday (2029-06-14): finish RCA draft and share a 1-page postmortem + decision on final credit amount.
- If you’d like, we can schedule a 30-minute review with engineering tomorrow to walk traces.

Marissa — please confirm whether the provisional credit formula and the 3.6% estimate match what billing expects to propose as a formal credit.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Reliability Analyst, Redwood Inference

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C4D5E6F
Attachments: proposed_credit_calc.xlsx

From: Jordan Lee <jordan@checkpoint.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Checkpoint Ops <ops@checkpoint.ai>
Date: 2029-06-14T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike during checkpoint fallback - request to validate window and credit

Laura / David / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the transparency. We reviewed the drive artifacts and your preliminary calc. A few quick notes from procurement:
- 3.6% looks directionally reasonable to us given the token-weighting and the window.
- We’d prefer a formal one-line postmortem (RCA) and the finalized credit calculation before routing for internal approval.

We’ll hold off on escalating but request the 1-page RCA and final credit number today if possible. If you need a signature/DocuSign for the credit apportionment, we can route it quickly — you can use the link below when ready.

DocuSign placeholder: https://app.docusign.com/doc/ABCDEFG12345

Appreciate the partnership — happy to hop on a short call to close this out.

Best,
Jordan Lee
Head of Platform, Checkpoint AI

Attachment: ops@checkpoint.ai logs referenced earlier (provided separately)
